newsitem.title: USA: Dow bursts through 7800 in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Dow bursts through 7800 in late trading.

text.p: U.S. stocks barreled higher into record territory in late trading on Thursday with the Dow Jones industrial average brushing the 7800 mark for the first time ever.
The 30-stock blue chip average was up 81 to 7800 in late trading amid bullishness on Wall Street that overcame a stronger-than-expected report on the economy.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index was up ten to 899.11, also in record territory.

Several analysts said the gains were reflective of the pervasive bullish mood on Wall Street, which was boosted this morning, when Prudential market analyst Ralph Acompora raised his already-high targets for the Dow to 10,000 in one year.
"A lot of this is triple-witching," said one trader, referring to tomorrow's simulataneous expiration of futures and indexes.
"A lot of people are short out there ... and they have to buy stock to replace them when they expire, that's causing a run-up," he said.
The long bond was up 2/32 to yield 6.73 percent.
